en.name: Pistachios
en.summary: Pistachios keep 3 weeks from purchase in the cupboard, 12 months in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and 24 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). The same record adds a caveat worth repeating: it considers refrigerating or freezing pistachios to provide no benefit, on the reasonable assumption that a bag gets eaten long before the cupboard window runs out.
en.pantry: 3 weeks from purchase, sealed, cool, dark and dry, whether the nuts are in the shell or not. Pistachios are less oily than pecans or macadamias, but they are still a nut, and the fat is what eventually turns. Roasted and salted ones also go soft in a humid kitchen, since salt pulls moisture out of the air. Clip the bag or decant into a jar, and keep them away from the hob and out of direct sun.
en.fridge: 12 months from purchase at 4 °C (40 °F) or below in an airtight container. Note that the record itself says refrigeration provides no benefit — read that as a comment on habit rather than on chemistry. For a bag you will finish in a few weeks, the cupboard genuinely is enough. For a kilo bought at a good price, cold slows the oil down and keeps pantry moths out, and the figure above is what you get.
en.freezer: 24 months from purchase at −18 °C (0 °F), with the same caveat attached: the record regards freezing as providing no benefit for normal quantities. It does no harm — pistachios hold little water, so texture is unaffected — and it is the right call for a bulk buy. Bag them airtight with the air pressed out and let the bag warm sealed before opening.
en.thawing: No thawing needed. Let a chilled or frozen bag come back to room temperature while still closed, so condensation does not soften the nuts or the shells.
spoilage: A bitter, sharp or paint-like taste, which is rancid oil.
Shells that are stained or blotchy, or kernels that look dull and grey-green rather than bright.
Soft, chewy nuts instead of crisp ones — moisture from a humid kitchen.
A musty smell, or mould inside a shell that got damp.
tips: Buy in the quantity you will eat; for most households the cupboard window is plenty.
Chill or freeze only a bulk purchase, and seal it properly if you do.
Salted pistachios soften fastest — an airtight jar matters more for those.
Shells that have not split contain no kernel worth the effort; discard them rather than forcing them.

faq.a: 3 weeks from purchase in the cupboard, 12 months in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or 24 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F).

faq.q: Do pistachios need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: The record says refrigeration provides no benefit, meaning a normal bag is eaten well within the cupboard window. Cold still helps a bulk purchase, and the figures above apply if you use it.

faq.q: How can you tell if pistachios have gone bad?
faq.a: Eat one. Rancid pistachios are bitter and taste of old oil. Softness on its own is moisture, and a musty smell means the bag goes.

zh.name: 開心果
zh.summary: 開心果自購買日起放櫥櫃 3 週，4 °C 以下冷藏 12 個月，−18 °C 冷凍 24 個月。同一份資料另外加了一句值得轉述的但書：它認為把開心果冷藏或冷凍「沒有額外好處」，理由也合理——一包開心果通常遠在櫥櫃期限到期前就被吃完了。
zh.pantry: 密封、陰涼、避光、乾燥，自購買日起 3 週，帶殼或去殼都一樣。開心果的油脂沒有胡桃或夏威夷豆那麼高，但終究是堅果，最後出問題的還是油。烘過加鹽的版本在濕熱的廚房還會變軟，因為鹽會把空氣中的水吸過來。請把袋口夾緊或倒進罐子，遠離爐台、避免直曬。
zh.fridge: 氣密容器放 4 °C 以下，自購買日起 12 個月。請注意，資料本身寫的是冷藏沒有額外好處——把那句話當成對「使用習慣」的評論，而不是對化學的評論。幾週內吃得完的一包，櫥櫃真的就夠了。但如果是趁特價買了一公斤，低溫會拖慢油脂變化、也擋掉穀蛾，而你拿到的就是上面這個數字。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下，自購買日起 24 個月，同樣附著那句但書：以一般用量而言，資料認為冷凍沒有額外好處。凍了不會有害——開心果含水少，質地不受影響——而大量採購時這就是對的做法。請壓出空氣密封裝袋，並且維持密封回溫再打開。
zh.thawing: 不需要解凍。冰過或凍過的請維持密封回到室溫，免得結露把果仁或殼弄軟。
spoilage: 嚐起來苦、尖銳或有油漆味，那是油耗。
殼上有污斑，或果仁顏色暗沉灰綠而不是鮮亮。
果仁軟韌不脆——那是濕熱廚房帶來的水氣。
有霉味，或受潮的殼裡面長霉。
tips: 買吃得完的量；對多數家庭來說櫥櫃的窗口綽綽有餘。
只有大量採購才需要冷藏或冷凍，要做就確實密封。
加鹽的開心果最快變軟，氣密罐對它更重要。
沒有裂口的殼裡通常不值得硬撬，直接丟掉比較省事。

faq.a: 自購買日起，放櫥櫃 3 週，4 °C 以下冷藏 12 個月，−18 °C 冷凍 24 個月。
資料寫的是冷藏沒有額外好處，意思是一般份量會在櫥櫃期限內吃完。大量採購時低溫仍然有幫助，要用的話就適用上面的數字。
吃一顆。油耗的開心果會苦、有久放的油味。單純變軟只是受潮；有霉味則整包都要丟。
